1.explanation:
Both files handle how User Timing entries get collected and shown in the final report. 

• lighthouse-core/audits/user-timings.js is responsible for reading the raw User Timing entries from the artifact and turning them into the audit’s result object. It currently passes through the entry.startTime values unfiltered, so any negative times arrive here and end up in the audit’s output. 

• lighthouse-core/formatters/partials/user-timings.js is responsible for rendering those entries in the HTML/JSON report. Since it simply iterates over the audit.result.details.items and prints startTime.toFixed(2), negative numbers remain visible to users. 

Fixing this bug will involve either filtering out or clamping negative startTime values in the audit code (user-timings.js) or adjusting the formatter (user-timings.js partial) to skip or normalize negative times before display.
1.bug_scenario: When running Lighthouse (either via the CLI or the Chrome extension) on a page that injects User Timing marks before the NavigationStart (for example, by using Puppeteer’s page.evaluateOnNewDocument to call performance.mark()), the audit output (“Performance → User Timing marks and measures”) shows negative startTime values for those early marks (e.g. “Mark: -184.69ms – mark_features_unveil_start”). These negative offsets occur because the marks are recorded before the trace’s zero-point (NavigationStart), and neither the audit logic nor the formatting logic filters them out or normalizes them to zero.

2.explanation: Both of these files are responsible for collecting and rendering the User Timing entries in Lighthouse. The audit implementation (lighthouse-core/audits/user-timings.js) pulls raw PerformanceEntry objects (including startTime) directly from the driver artifact without clamping negative times. The formatter (lighthouse-core/formatters/user-timings.js) then displays those startTime values verbatim in the report UI. Together they expose the negative offsets instead of normalizing them to zero or otherwise handling pre-navigation marks.
2.bug_scenario: When running Lighthouse (or the DevTools “User Timings” extension) on a page where scripts insert performance.marks before the browser’s NavigationStart event (for example via Puppeteer’s evaluateOnNewDocument), those early marks appear with negative startTime values relative to zero. Lighthouse currently surfaces and formats these negative offsets in the User Timings audit, leading to entries like “-184.69ms – mark_features_unveil_start.”
